symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions on leaves with gray/white centers
Dark brown reddish borders on leaf blades
Node necrosis and neck rot preventing grain filling
Stunted crop growth and partial panicle drying
organic_treatment: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/liter of water or Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) every 7 days. Incorporate trichoderma viride in compost.
chemical_treatment: Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5ml/L of water at boot leaf stage.
preventive_measures: Avoid excess nitrogenous fertilizers (split application recommended)
Maintain 2-5 cm standing water during tillering
Use resistant varieties like Swarna-Sub1 or IR-64
Destroy infected crop stubbles after harvest
irrigation_advisory: Avoid continuous deep flooding; practice alternate wetting and drying (AWD) to reduce humidity around the canopy.
fertilizer_guidance: Reduce Urea by 25%. Apply Potash (MOP) @ 20kg/acre to strengthen cell walls against fungal penetration.

regional_guidance.North: High risk in Punjab & Haryana during high humidity (Aug-Sep). Ensure early evening field drainage.
regional_guidance.South: Common in Godavari delta and Cauvery belt. Monitor closely during Samba season.
regional_guidance.East: Prevalent in West Bengal & Odisha during wet season (Aman rice). Use certified disease-free seeds.
regional_guidance.West: High incidence in Konkan belt. Apply prophylactic biocontrol agents at nursery stage.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark green/black lesions starting at leaf tips and margins
White cottony fungal growth on lower leaf surfaces under high humidity
Browning and rapid rotting of green and mature fruits
Foul odor emitting from heavily infected foliage
organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture (1%) or Copper Hydroxide @ 2g/L. Spray diluted cow butter-milk (1:10 ratio) containing active lactic microbes.
chemical_treatment: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2g/L water.
preventive_measures: Ensure proper plant spacing (60cm x 45cm) for air circulation
Staking of plants to keep leaves off damp soil
Remove and burn lower infected leaves immediately
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation
irrigation_advisory: Use drip irrigation strictly in early morning hours so foliage dries quickly before nightfall.
fertilizer_guidance: Apply Calcium Nitrate @ 5kg/acre via fertigation to strengthen cell walls and prevent fruit decay.

regional_guidance.North: Prevalent during foggy winter months (Nov-Jan) in UP, Bihar, and Himachal.
regional_guidance.South: High occurrence in Kolar (Karnataka) and Madanapalle (AP) during monsoon spells.
regional_guidance.East: Common in Ranchi plateau and Assam during persistent rainfall.
regional_guidance.West: Monitor closely in Nashik and Pune belts during October heat with high night humidity.

symptoms: Water-soaked angular spots bounded by leaf veins
Black vein lesions ('Black arm') leading to stem breakage
Dark sunken water-soaked spots on bolls ('Boll rot')
Premature leaf drop and boll shedding
organic_treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 10g/kg seed. Foliar spray of Garlic + Chili extract @ 5%.
chemical_treatment: Streptocycline 90% + Tetracycline 10% @ 6g + Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 500g in 200L water per acre.
preventive_measures: Delint seeds with Concentrated Sulphuric Acid before sowing
Use resistant Bt-Cotton hybrid varieties
Destroy previous crop residue and crop field sanitation
Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet
irrigation_advisory: Ensure good field drainage; avoid waterlogging around roots for more than 24 hours.
fertilizer_guidance: Balanced NPK (120:60:60 kg/ha). Avoid excessive Nitrogen which promotes succulent bacterial host tissue.

regional_guidance.North: Monitor in Malwa region of Punjab & Rajasthan during humid July-August.
regional_guidance.South: Common in Telangana & Rayalaseema black soils during early monsoon.
regional_guidance.East: Found in Odisha plateau cotton zones during erratic rainfall.
regional_guidance.West: Widespread in Vidarbha and Saurashtra; spray immediately after heavy rain breaks.

symptoms: Concentric ring brown spots ('Target board' pattern) on older leaves
Yellow halo surrounding brown necrotic leaf spots
Dry brown sunken spots on tuber skin
Early leaf senescense and defoliation
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of Neem oil (10,000 ppm) @ 3ml/L with liquid soap binder or Trichoderma harzianum soil drench.
chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Propineb 70% WP @ 2.0g/L water.
preventive_measures: Maintain crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (Maize/Legumes) for 2 years
Soil solarization before planting
Harvest tubers only after vine killing when skin is fully mature
Store tubers at 4°C with proper ventilation
irrigation_advisory: Irrigate in morning. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation late in the afternoon.
fertilizer_guidance: Ensure adequate Potassium and Zinc application; deficient plants are highly susceptible to Alternaria.

regional_guidance.North: Widespread in Indo-Gangetic plains (UP, West Bengal, Punjab) during Jan-Feb.
regional_guidance.South: Found in Nilgiris and Hassan potato tracts.
regional_guidance.East: Common in Hooghly district of West Bengal.

symptoms: Shot-hole leaf damage and ragged pinholes on young whorl leaves
Large quantities of saw-dust like excreta (frass) inside central leaf whorls
Defoliation of whorl leaves leaving only leaf midribs
Caterpillars with inverted 'Y' mark on head and 4 dark spots on tail segment
organic_treatment: Apply Metarhizium anisopliae or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2g/L into leaf whorls. Place sand/sawdust mixed with neem powder into central whorls.
chemical_treatment: Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4ml/L targeted inside leaf whorls.
chemical_dosage_per_acre: 80g Emamectin Benzoate in 200L water per acre
preventive_measures: Erect Pheromone traps @ 5/acre for moth monitoring
Intercropping with Cowpea, Desmodium or Push-Pull push legumes
Early uniform sowing across entire village cluster
Handpick and destroy egg masses covered with hair scale
irrigation_advisory: Heavy whorl irrigation can drown early instar larvae inside central leaf funnel.
fertilizer_guidance: Basal NPK dose (120:60:40 kg/ha). Avoid excess split nitrogen during peak infestation.

regional_guidance.North: Widespread across Bihar, UP, and Rajasthan maize fields.
regional_guidance.South: High density in Davangere (Karnataka) and Guntur (AP).
regional_guidance.East: Prevalent in Odisha tribal maize belts.

symptoms: Bright yellow pustules (uredinia) arranged in long linear stripes along leaf veins
Yellow powder rubbing off easily on fingers when touching infected leaves
Leaves turning brown, dry, and papery prematurely
Significant reduction in grain weight and shriveled seeds
organic_treatment: Spray fermented garlic-onion extract (5%) or Bio-agent Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L at first appearance of yellow stripes.
chemical_treatment: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L or Tebuconazole 250 EC @ 1ml/L water immediately upon spot detection.
chemical_dosage_per_acre: 200ml Propiconazole 25 EC in 200L water per acre
preventive_measures: Grow rust-resistant wheat varieties like DBW 187, HD 3226, or PBW 725
Avoid late sowing of wheat (sow before 15th November)
Destroy wild canary grass (Phalaris minor) and weed hosts around field borders
Regular morning scouting during cold humid spells
irrigation_advisory: Avoid over-irrigation during foggy weather; maintain optimum soil moisture without canopy wetness.
fertilizer_guidance: Split application of Nitrogen. Do not exceed recommended dose as excess N soft tissue favors rust spores.

regional_guidance.North: Critical threat in Punjab, Haryana, Himachal foothills, and Western UP.
regional_guidance.South: Rare in deep south; confined to high altitude Nilgiri hills.
regional_guidance.East: Occurs sporadically in Tarai region of Bihar.

symptoms: Vibrant green leaf coloration with uniform texture
No visible spots, lesions, chlorosis, or necrotic patches
Strong erect stem and healthy root system
Normal cell turgidity and growth vigor
organic_treatment: Maintain current good agricultural practices (GAP). Apply Jeevamrut or Panchagavya @ 3% as routine booster every 15 days.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment required. Protect natural beneficial predatory insects (ladybird beetles, green lacewings).
preventive_measures: Continue regular crop scouting every 3-5 days
Maintain balanced crop nutrition based on Soil Health Card
Practice crop rotation with legumes to build soil nitrogen
Keep field borders clean of weeds
irrigation_advisory: Irrigate based on soil moisture tensiometer reading (25-30% available soil moisture).
fertilizer_guidance: Follow customized Soil Health Card recommendations for N-P-K-Micronutrients.
